topic.reason: הנושא נקבע בתוכנית השבועית (חבילה 5 מתוך 7, כל חבילה על נושא אחר). כיבוי מסך הוא רגע של כל ערב ואין כאן טענה על תאריך. יש עליו מקורות טובים שנקראו היום: האקדמיה האמריקאית לרפואת ילדים (עמוד של ד״ר ג׳ני רדסקי), מחקר של אוניברסיטת וושינגטון על 28 משפחות, Common Sense Media בשיתוף Child Mind Institute ו-The Conversation. בקטלוג אין ספר על מסכים, אבל באתר אפשר ליצור סיפור חדש, ויש את הדובי משנה צבעים (גילאי 2 עד 6) על זיהוי רגשות כמו כעס, לקישור בהודעה.

voice.note: קול מכויל: 37 דוגמאות מאושרות מתוך העריכות של ירין. הכתיבה לפי שינויי העריכה האחרונים (דוגמה אחת בשקופית כשאפשר, סיכום קצר בלי רשימת נקודות).

sources.title: Screen Time & Temper Tantrums: Helpful Tips for Parents
sources.publisher: HealthyChildren.org, American Academy of Pediatrics (by Jenny Radesky, MD, FAAP; last updated 3/13/2024)
sources.quote: Advance planning can prevent struggles, but it won't eliminate every meltdown. ... You can help build a bridge back to reality by entering the room or sitting down near your child, quietly observing what they're doing. When you see signs that they're willing to engage, offer a warm smile of encouragement. ... This isn't the time to go over the rules, since a child in meltdown mode can't think logically. Simply hold your ground, using as few words as possible: "I know it's tough, but it's time to put your tablet away." ... Kids can benefit from having a spot where they can go to calm down. ... If your child starts to rage when screen time ends, ask them to go to their quiet spot until they feel better. If necessary, gently pick up a younger child or lead them by the hand. Tell them you'll be glad to see them again when they're ready to reconnect. ... Try it with younger kids, too: offer a beloved book, cuddle time with the family pet or a small chore that makes them feel part of the group.
sources.supports: Advance planning can prevent struggles but won't eliminate every meltdown; sit down near the child, watch what they do and smile; few words and holding your ground; a quiet spot, leading a younger child by the hand, glad to see them when ready; trading up to a pet cuddle, a small chore or a beloved book. Fragments read in the page today, joined with ' ... '.

sources.title: Two-minute warnings make kids’ ‘screen time’ tantrums worse
sources.publisher: UW News, University of Washington (Jennifer Langston, May 5, 2016; on Hiniker, Suh, Cao and Kientz, CHI 2016)
sources.quote: Some things did make that switch easier, like having routines, disengaging at a natural stopping point or simply having a battery die. But children aged 1 to 5 who were given a two-minute warning by their parents were more upset when the screen went away. ... Natural stopping points in the content children were viewing or in the games they were interacting with made transitions easier
sources.supports: A natural stopping point made the switch easier in a diary study of families with children aged 1 to 5. Fragments read in the page today, joined with ' ... '.

sources.title: How do I put a stop to screen time (turn off the TV or take the phone away) without causing a meltdown?
sources.publisher: Common Sense Media (the Child Mind Institute contributed; last reviewed or updated September 27, 2021)
sources.quote: Have a plan. Explain beforehand to your kid that he or she can watch a certain number of shows or for a specific time period. Let them know what to expect after the show, too. ... Turn it off and stick to your guns.
sources.supports: Explain beforehand how many shows and what comes after; turn it off and stick to your guns. Fragments read in the page today, joined with ' ... '.

sources.title: 3 ways to help your child transition off screens and avoid the dreaded ‘tech tantrums’
sources.publisher: The Conversation (Juliana Zabatiero, Kate Highfield, Leon Straker and Susan Edwards; published January 9, 2024)
sources.quote: Some successful strategies parents and carers in this research used were “you can watch two episodes of this show” or “when this game is finished we will stop”. ... Telling them what activity would follow was also helpful. For example “when you have finished that game it will be time to eat” or “after you have watched that show we will go to the park”. What they are moving to may not always be fun, helping children understand what to expect helps make for a smoother transition.
sources.supports: 'You can watch two episodes of this show' and saying what activity follows helped families in a 12 week study. Fragments read in the page today, joined with ' ... '.

claims.wording_he: רוב העבודה קורית לפני שהמסך נדלק
claims.supports: AAP: advance planning can prevent struggles, but it won't eliminate every meltdown (so the slide says 'חלק מהמריבות').

claims.wording_he: לסכם מראש כמה פרקים ומה אחרי
claims.supports: The Conversation: 'you can watch two episodes of this show' and telling them what activity would follow; Common Sense Media: explain beforehand how many shows and what to expect after.
AAP: sit down near your child, quietly observe what they're doing, offer a warm smile; it builds a bridge back to the here and now.
UW: natural stopping points in the content made transitions easier.

claims.wording_he: משפט אחד בלי הרצאה והטאבלט לא חוזר
claims.supports: AAP: don't lecture; hold your ground with as few words as possible ('I know it's tough, but it's time to put your tablet away'); Common Sense Media: stick to your guns.
AAP: a quiet spot until they feel better; if necessary lead a younger child by the hand; tell them you'll be glad to see them when they're ready ('אחכה לך פה' is our wording).

claims.wording_he: לעבור למשהו שהיא אוהבת עוד יותר
claims.supports: AAP 'trading up': cuddle time with the family pet or a small chore.

claims.wording_he: תכנון לפני ומעט מילים ברגע עצמו
claims.supports: A recap of slides 2 to 8, each with its source.
HealthyChildren.org (AAP) suggests 'trading up' when the screen ends, and for younger kids names 'a beloved book' first. That the story is personalised, with the child as the hero, is our wording.
The child's name is in the text and the child stars in every illustration; parents can pick a catalogue story or create a new one (live site, 24 Oct 2026). No brand or title on the slide.
